Bahesti Marjan, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 

Md Golam Mostafa, Advocate—For the Opposite Party No. 1.
parties:
Hasen Ali and others ---------- Petitioners
Vs.
Ayesha Khatun Bibi and others ------------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-7-2004 and 5-8-2004 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh in Other Appeal No. 27 of 2001affirming the judgment decree dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge Sadar, Mymensingh in Other Case No. 261 of 1991 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts for disposal of the Rule are that the instant revisional application has arisen against the judgment dated 29-7-2004 and decree dated 5-8-2004 passed by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Class Appeal No. 27 of 2001 affirming the judgment dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh in Other Case No. 261 of 1991.

3. The opposite party No.1 instituted the Other suit being No. 261 of 1991 seeking the following reliefs:

সে মতে প্রার্থনা যে,

(ক) নালিশী তপশিলস্থ ভূমিতে ক্রয়সূত্রে বাদিনীর স্বত্ত্ব ও স্বার্থ থাকা মর্মে বাদিনীর অনুকুলে এবং বিবাদীগনের প্রতিকূলে এক স্বত্ব ঘোষনার ডিক্রী দিতে,

(খ)বিবাদীগণ স্বেচ্ছায় দখল না ছাড়িলে নালিশী তপশিলস্থ ভূমিতে বিবাদীগণের উত্তোলিত গৃহাদি সমূহ অপসারন পূর্বক বিবাদীগণকে উচ্ছেদক্রমে তৎস্থলে বাদিনীকে আদালত যোগে দখল দিবার জন্য বাদিনীর অনুকুলে এবং বিবাদীগনের প্রতিকূলে ডিক্রী দিতে,

4.  The suit of the opposite party No.1 plaintiff in short is that the suit land is situated at Mouja Kustia under Sadar Upazilla, District Mymensingh the CS Plot No. 684 was originally belonged to one late Naimuddin, the father of petitioner No. 1 and 2 and one Zinnat Ali who became the owner and possessor of the suit land by inheritance from their ancestral, and by purchase Zinnat Ali transferred 3 decimals of land to the plaintiff and on 22-7-1975 vide registered deed No. 22683 Naimuddin transferred 6.50 decimals of land vide registered deed No. 15620 to plaintiff dated 22-10-1975. Since purchase plaintiff planted 60 betel nut trees, their age is 7 years and before 3/4 years planted 4 mango trees, four jackfruit trees, two Jamrul trees, one Amra tree, all these are available there, defendants are trying to enter into the suit premises and to destroy those. Due to car accident the husband of the plaintiff was sentenced and was in jail hajat and the plaintiff was in bed ridden. On 1st Shraban 1397 BS Mojibur Rahman and Mofazzal erected a tin shed house and others defendants erected four katcha house (Chaner Ghar). The defendants erected those houses forcefully. So the plaintiff instituted suit for declaration and to evict the defendants and to deliver the possession of the suit land to plaintiff. 5. The defendant No. 1, 2 and 3 filed a written statement and defendant No.4 now the petitioner No.3 also filed a separate written statement denying the contention made in the plaint and defendant No.4 now the petitioner No.3 stated in his written statement that on 25-2-1976 vide registered deed serial No. 3636 and deed No. 3643, his brother Mujibur Rahman purchased 4 decimals of land from CS Plot No. 684 corresponding to DP Khatian No. 1278 DP Plot No. 2891. The brother of the defendant No. 4 now the petitioner No. 3 erected a tin shed house and a katcha house (Chaner ghar) and by growing different kinds of trees have been enjoying its peaceful possession since purchase without interruption from any quarter, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 never possessed the suit land just to grab the land of the defendant No.4 now petitioner No.3 has filed the false fabricated, cooked up and vexatious suit against the petitioner the plaintiff has no and had no right, title, interest and possession over the 4 decimals of land of the defendant. The suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. The suit property 4 decimals of land is a homestead and the brother of the defendant No. 4 i.e. petitioner No.3 has been living with family members by erecting tin shed and katcha ghar (Chaner Ghar) therein.

6. The defendant No.1 and 2 now the petitioner No.1 and 2 filed a written statement denying the contention of the plaint and stating that the suit property was originally belonged to their father Naimuddin and Naimuddin died, leaving behind his heirs this defendant and others. During the life time of Naimuddin they had been living in the suit land with family members as homestead. Naimuddin did not transfer 6.50 decimals of land from the suit plot to the plaintiff and no question arise regarding delivery of possession of the suit land to the plaintiff. After the death of Naimuddin after 13 or 15 years the plaintiff instituted the false and fabricated suit showing a false deed which was not executed and registered by Naimuddin in favour of the plaintiff. The so-called deed is fully denied by the defendant-petitioners. During DP Khatian operation the names of the defendants-petitioners were correctly recorded in DP Khatian.

7. Ms Beheshti Marjan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners while Mr Md Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. Ms Beheshti Marjan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, did not apply his judicial mind both law and facts, by considering the materials on record, evidences on record and exhibits No. 2 and 3, came to an erroneous findings and decision which is slipshod, surmises, arbitrary, fanciful, hypothesis, it is liable to be set-aside.

9. She further submits that both the learned trial judge and appellate judge did not consider in their findings and decisions of the impugned judgment and orders that the contention of the plaint and the evidence of the plaintiff is contradictory, falsehood, cooked up. They came to an erroneous findings and decisions, their judgments are slipshod, fanciful, and arbitrary, it is liable to be set-aside.

10. She further submits that the deed writers of suit deeds exhibits 2 and 3 were not examined. If they died, their death certificates were not produced before the trial court or appellate Courts. The attesting witness of suit deeds exhibit 2 and 3, Yusuf Ali, Abul Kalam, Motiur Rahman were not examined, the fathers name and address of PW 8 Md Abul Mansur is not written in the deed (Exhibit-2) non examination of attesting witness and vital witness it creates doubt regarding execution and registration of suit deeds exhibit 2 and 3. No witness deposed before the learned trial judge that they saw Md Naimuddin and Zinnat Ali Munshi appeared before the concerning Sub registry office to submit the deeds for registration before the Sub register and put their left thumb impression (LTI) in the volume of concern registry office on the date of so called registration dated 22-7-1975 and 22-10-1975. The impugned judgments are slipshod, surmise, occasioning failure of justice, liable to be set-aside.

11. She further submits that in the impugned judgment the learned trial judge and appellate judges committed an error in their findings and decisions regarding possession of the plaintiff. The plaintiff stated in the plaint at paragraph No. 3 that after purchase on 22-7-1975 and 22-10-1975 to 1-8-1991 there is about 16 years, the age of 7 years of nut trees are quite doubtful, plaintiff admitted in her examination in cross that she planted trees in the early year of 1975 is quite doubtful. No witness deposed regarding the measurement of suit land after so called registration of deeds and nobody also deposed that Naimuddin and Zinnat Ali delivered the possession of suit land after the so called execution and registration, infavour of the plaintiff, the impugned judgments and decrees are slipshod and liable to be set-aside.

12. She further submitted that the plaintiff stated that she dispossessed on 1st Shraban 1397 BS i.e. 17-9-1990 of Christian Era, she instituted the suit on 1-8-1991 near about 1 year, she did not disclose anything regarding the late of filing suit after so called dispossession from the suit land, no GD entry is made or no criminal case is instituted, no local salish was held and the plaintiff did not seek relief under section 9 of Specific Relief Act for restoration of possession, no Medical certificate for illness of plaintiff or no documents regarding the sentence of plaintiffs husband was exhibited before the learned trial judge or appellate judge, plaintiff stated she was dispossessed at the noon of 1397 BS but PW 4 stated house was built in the morning, PW 7 stated plaintiff was dispossessed at 10.30 am on the date of so called dispossession PW 7 stated plaintiff register the dispossession, plaintiff admitted she was in bed ridden, the statements are contradictory PW 7 admitted that in the suit land there is dwelling house and a kitchen house of Naimuddin and PW 4 admitted that there is no house in the suit land now, the learned courts below committed an error in their findings and decisions in the impugned judgments and decrees resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice, it is contradictory and liable to be set-aside.

13. She has also added that the depositions of DW 1, DW 2, DW 3, DW 4, DW 5 and DW 6 were not denied by plaintiff, DW 1 clearly stated they did not dispossess the plaintiff, they lived their father's house since livelihood of their father and their father died in the suit land. Their father did not execute the so called deed on 19-10-1975, there is a graveyard in the suit land, plaintiff never possessed the suit land. The statements of PWs are contradictory. There is corroborating evidence of DWs. The learned trial judge and appellate judges committed an error in discussing the deposition of DWs resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice, it is liable to be set-aside.

14. The learned Advocate lastly submits that PW 6 clearly stated that there is different in left thumb impression of suit deeds with the left thumb impression of record of Sub registry office, he is the so called identifier of executor, Naimuddin. P.W. 3 is hearsay witness PW 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are interested witness, the statements are contradictory. The impugned judgment and orders suffers error of law, it is needless to prove the limitation by the defendants as per provision under section 56 of the Evidence Act. The learned trial judge and appellate judges committed an error in their findings and decision, occasioning failure of justice.

15. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in support of her contentions has referred the following case, such as the case of Abul Hossain vs Amjad Hossain, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 437, the case of Gopinath Das vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 64 DLR 167, the case of Md Mozaffer Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 15 MLR (AD) 170, the case of Md Amzad Hossain Parag vs. Md Saiful Islam, reported in 9 ADC 224. She lastly referred the case of Md Hossain Mia vs Shujayatullah, reported in 36 DLR 191.

16. Mr Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submits that both the parties admit that Naimudin and Jinnat Ali were owners and possessors of the suit land. The said Naimuddin on 22-7-1975 through Saf-kabala deed No. 22683 sold 3 decimals of suit land to the plaintiff and delivered the possession of the same and late Jinnat Ali on 22-10-1975 through Saf-kabala deed 15620 sold 6.50 decimal of the suit land to the plaintiff and delivered possession to the plaintiff and in this way the plaintiff was owner and possessor of 9.50 decimals of suit land.

17. The learned Advocate further submits that it is submitted that PW 8 Abdul Mansur identified the Vendor (Jinnat Ali) of the deed by exhibiting the deed No. 22683 dated 22-7-1975 as Exhibit 2 (Ka) and PW 6 Md Kalu identified the vendor (Naimuddin) of deed No. 15620 dated 22-10-1975 and exhibited the deed being exhibit No. 3 and this witness also deposes that the vendor is his "Talai" and the deed was written in front of him and the same was read out to the vendor and the said Naimuddin called this witness to be witness in the deed and also deposes that the plaintiff paid consideration money to Naimuddin who after receipt of the same executed and registered the deed. The PW 2 has clearly deposed the plaintiff purchased the suit land from Nazimuddin and Jinnat Ali in 1975 and got possession of the same and she planted so many trees in the suit land but the defendants dispossessed her from the suit and built houses thereon.

18. He further submits that PW 2 Hurmat Ali, PW 4 Jalaluddin and PW 7 Noor Hossain deposed in the court and supported the case of plaintiff and denied the contents of the defendants. The plaintiff by oral and documentary evidences could well proved her case i.e. purchases of the suit land and got the possession of the same and was in physical possession and enjoying the same by planting several trees on the suit land and lastly she dispossessed by the defendants from the suit land.

19. He further submits that the defendants No. 1 and 2 sons of late Naimuddin contested the suit and DW 1 Hashem Ali son of Naimuddin deposed in the Court but did not claim that his father did not execute the Deed or put thumb impression in the said deed as in exhibit No. 3 and more over in cross-examination stated also that he does not know anything about this sale. DW 2 and DW 3 does not depose anything regarding the execution of the sale deed.

20. He lastly submits that the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 contested the suit by filing written statement stating that on 25-7-1976 they purchased 4 decimals of suit land from Taleb Ali who got the properties from Jinnat Ali (The father of defendant Nos. 4 and 6) by Ewaz Badal on the same day. But none of his witnesses deposed nothing regarding delivery of possession of the said land and, as such, the Ewaz Badal was not acted upon have no legal effect DW 4 witnesses for defendant No. 4 in cross-examination stated that he does not know whether Jinnat Ali sold the said land to the plaintiff earlier than their purchase and in this way the purchase of the suit land by the plaintiff through two deeds exhibited Nos. 2 and 3 were well proved.

21. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties in support of his contentions has referred the following case, such as the case of Joynal Abedin vs Hafizur Rahman reported in 13 BLD (AD) 150 = 44 DLR (AD) 162, in the case of Chairman, Mongla Port Authority vs Kazi Brothers, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 9, in the case of Mahmud Ali vs Bangladesh reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 56, in the case of Abdus Samad Khan vs Wazedali Fakir, reported in 44 DLR 495, in the case of Md Shah Alam vs Musammat Farida Begum, reported in 2 MLR (AD) 153 = 2 BLC (AD) 92, in the case of Mohammad Yeasin Khan vs Deputy Commissioner; Brahmanbaria, reported in 2 MLR (AD) 211, in the case of Sadaruddin Miah vs Abdul Mannaf Mia, reported in 3 MLR (AD) 22, in the case of Government of Bangladesh represented by the Additional Deputy Commissioner vs Abdul Hoque Khan, reported in 3 MLR (AD) 255. He lastly referred the case of Haiderunnessa vs Monowara Begum reported in 16 BLD (AD) 280.

22. I have perused the impugned judgment dated 29-7-2004 and decree dated 5-8-2004 passed by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Appeal No. 27 of 2001 affirming the judgment dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 passed by the learned senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Mymensingh in Other case No. 261 of 1991.

23. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the revisional application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

24. Before arriving at a proper finding it is utmost important to go through the citations as referred by the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners first of all I would like to go through the case of Abul Hossain vs Amjad Hossain reported in 62 DLR (AD) 436 where our Apex Court held that—

"Section 110 of the Evidence Act provides for a presumption of ownership in favour of the person who is in possession of the property. A person in possession of land however imperfect his title may be, has a good title against whole world except the true owner and until the true owner comes in Court to assert a claim to the property. Possession is evidence of title, and gives a good title as against wrong doer."

"The High Court Division in the premises fell in an error in reversing the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge without adverting to the findings arrived at as regards acquisition title and possession of the suit lands by the appellants. On consideration of the fact and circumstances of the matter, we are of the view that the High Court Division erred in law in disbelieving the appellants title in the suit lands."

25. In the case of Gopinath Das, vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 64 DLR 167 where it is held that—

"Initiation of suit is not seen by the superior Courts as an unrestricted right to be exercised at pleasure. It must disclose a cause of action' within the meaning of 'right as to any property' or 'legal character' so far as section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is concerned."

26. In the case of Md Mozaffer Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 15 MLR (AD) 170, where our Apex Court held that—

"Suit for declaration of title in the absence of satisfactory proof thereof is not maintainable—

In the instant case the plaintiffs could not prove their title to the suit land by producing documentary evidence as well as oral evidence. The trial court dismissed the suit on specific finding which the court of Appeal, High Court Division and the Appellate Division held perfectly justified."

27. It appears that the trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal below on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary found that the plaintiffs could not prove their right and title in the suit land, it appears that in the instant case, the plaintiffs claimed their predecessor-in-interest became tenant of the suit land by way of pattan as well as oral gift but at the trial the plaintiff could not prove neither the story of pattan nor the oral gift by adducing any reliable or documentary evidence. It also appears that the plaintiffs had no title to the suit land and the story of pattan as well as oral gift is false. Accordingly, both the Courts below rightly and correctly arrived at a finding that the plaintiffs failed to establish their right and title in the suit land.

28. In the case of Md Amzad Hossain Parag vs Md Saiful Islam, reported in 9 ADC 224 where it is held that—

The Specific Relief Act, 1877, section 42 Declaration of Kabla deed collusive and forged Onus of proof lies upon.

"The trial court, on consideration of evidence adduced by the contesting parties and other facts and circumstances, dismissed the suit by the judgment and order dated 17-4-2004 holding mainly that the plaintiffs could not prove the case that the impugned kabala deed was forged, collusive etc. The trial Court also found that the contesting defendants have been possessing the suit land in recording the same in their names and on payment of rent since their purchase."

29. In the case of Md Hossain Mia vs Shujayatullah, reported in 36 DLR 191 where it is held that—

Presumption- possession goes with title.

30. It the evidence of possession on behalf of the plaintiffs and on behalf of the defendants as to the farmer's possession within 12 years before suit is evenly balanced the presumption that possession goes with title shall prevail; where the evidence adduced by both the parties, although unsatisfactory is not altogether valueless, the court is entitled to take into consideration the presumption arises from title.

<u>31. The presumptive possession of the plaintiffs in the land on proof of their title in the facts of the case would be sufficient to discharge the onus of proving possession because presumption is an inference as to existence of a fact from the existence of some other founded fact.</u>

32. In view of the attending facts and circumstances and the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocates of both the sides and citations as referred in support of their respective contentions I find merit in the submissions of the learned advocate for the petitioners and the citations as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners in support of her contention are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

33. On the other hand, the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties is devoid of any substance and the citations as referred by him have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case,

34. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds.

35. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

36. The impugned judgment dated 29-7-2004 and decree dated 5-8-2004 passed by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh, in Other Appeal No. 27 of 2001 affirming the impugned judgment dated 27-11-2000 and decree dated 30-11-2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Mymensingh in Other case No. 261 of 1991 is hereby set-aside.

37. The order of stay granted earlier at the time issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

The office is directed to communicate the judgment to the concerned Court below and send down the lower Court's records at once.

End.
